blocks.text: PDS wave 45 - the price column learns to expire

content.value: STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. GROUND TRUTH, DERIVED IN-PROCESS at origin/main ab8c86b05 in a detached worktree, never the primary checkout (which is stale at a31faa52d and dirty across eight charters). I ran scripts/pds-door-census.sh myself: rc=0, ERRORS 0, every program disposed. THE HEADLINE THE WISH DID NOT ASK FOR: the census runs in 4.13 s wall / 2.80 s CPU - so it CANNOT have taken the 40.33 s CPU / 68.24 s wall figure it prints. Every price and every disposition-evidence string is a hardcoded literal in PDS_DOOR_PRICES (:146-149) and PDS_DOOR_DISPOSITIONS (:123-137). The CLASS column became an instrument in wave 44. The PRICE column became a shell variable with a date stamp. And the denominator is 20 with 4 doors, not the 19 with 3 that both the wish and the lead notes carry - the census counts itself, and says so at :12-14.

blocks.text: The three blind spots, and why two of them are this wave's own doing

content.value: The census has exactly one rot check, at :585-602, and it tests EXISTENCE: a ledger row naming a file that is no longer on disk is an error. That catches deletion. It cannot catch the three shapes that actually rot a price column.

items.value: STALE PRICE. No content hash, no date arithmetic, no re-measurement. pds-record-parity.test.sh will print CPU=4.45s after someone doubles the harness's work, forever, and nothing reds.
STALE DISPOSITION EVIDENCE. Five rows cite "by run 2026-08-03: <cmd> rc=N". The census never re-takes any of them. A disposition survives its own repair.

ORPHANED DISPOSITION. Read the cond at :519-540: legA=yes AND legB=true short-circuits to THROUGH and the ledger is NEVER consulted. A disposition row for a now-THROUGH instrument is silently unread - not an error, not a warning, not printed.

content.value: THE COUPLING THAT MAKES THIS THE SPINE RATHER THAN A TANGENT: two of the three deferred slices the wish orders will make the census lie the day they land. pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door puts --selftest-offline through a rider plus ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - legA/legB then compute THROUGH and the ENVIRONMENT row at :128 becomes an unflagged orphan asserting a refusal that is no longer the disposition. pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication takes the sweep from rc=1 to rc=0 - and CONTENT-RED, evidenced by a run nobody re-takes, outlives the red it names. Price provenance is a PREREQUISITE for the wish's own item 2, not an addition to it.

blocks.text: The direction

content.value: The epic's law has walked one rung per wave. A receipt lies when the value it emits does not descend from the write return. A class lies when it does not descend from its substitution (wave 42). A gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce (wave 43). Wave 45's sentence is the one the new instrument earns:
A PRICE LIES WHEN IT DOES NOT DESCEND FROM A METER THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF DROVE - AND A DISPOSITION LIES WHEN ITS EVIDENCE NAMES A RUN THE INSTRUMENT NEVER RE-TAKES.

What the finished wave looks like: ./scripts/pds-door-census.sh still exits 0 on main and still costs seconds - it is a door, and its own 3.32 s row is its own gate cost, so any design that prices it out of its own door is disqualified before it is written. But every number it prints is now either taken by a meter it drove in THIS run, or a cached measurement carrying the content hash of the instrument it prices, so that a changed instrument turns the row PRICE-STALE and reds. A --measure verb takes the measurement and emits the exact ledger row, so re-pricing is one command rather than a hand ritual - the number descends from a meter the instrument drove, and anyone can re-take it. Dispositions whose evidence is a RUN get re-run under an opt-in, threshold-printed tier, so CONTENT-RED cannot survive its own repair. And an orphaned ledger row is an ERROR, because that is the exact shape both of this wave's own slices create.
Around that spine, the debts get paid at the new base. Priority order, and the reasoning behind it:

blocks.text: The direction debate

content.value: Three directions were developed far enough to cost something, then argued against each other.

blocks.text: Rival A - pay the debts, period

content.value: Do exactly the wish's items 1 through 5: three deferred slices, two owed reviews, the lv_verdict half, the criterion lesson. Do not touch the census - it exits 0, wave 44 declared it done, and reopening it is a fifth wave of arguing about a column. This is the disciplined reading of the brief and it has a real claim on the wave.

WHY IT LOSES: it hands the wave a false floor. Two of its own three slices silently corrupt the instrument, so "pay the debts" manufactures the next wave's finding. And it violates the mandate the user restates every single wave - DERIVE, NEVER TRANSCRIBE, INCLUDING FROM THIS BRIEF - by inheriting "the price column is an instrument now" as a premise instead of running it. I ran it. It is half an instrument, and the half that is prose is the half the column is named after.

blocks.text: Rival B - measure every price, every run

content.value: The pure fix: no cache, no ledger, no staleness possible. The census drives the meter for every row on every invocation and the price column is a measurement by construction.

WHY IT LOSES, on the epic's own evidence: D648 proved wall is not a property of a door on a shared host - a fixed workload's wall spanned 5.8x at constant load while its user CPU spanned 27 percent. A re-measuring census becomes the most expensive program in its own denominator: 40.33 s for pds-ledger-census_test.sh alone, plus the receipt census whose expensive arm D646 showed conceals ~140 s minimum from any outer meter. It would also have to price ITSELF - a fixpoint. Worst of all it converts a 4 s door into an ungateable one, killing the census's own THROUGH row, which is the single most self-defeating outcome available to this wave. The honest design is not "always measure" but "never assert a measurement you cannot re-take, and know when it expired."

blocks.text: Rival C - spend the column, gate the cheap doors

content.value: Take the census output at face value and do the obvious thing the wish's title demands - SPEND IT. Put every affordable row through the required gate: hetzner offline at 2.15 s, pds-record-parity.test.sh at 4.45 s, pds-scratch-target_test.sh at 8.91 s. Maximum visible progress, and it is exactly what four waves of arguing were FOR.

WHY IT LOSES AS A WHOLE DIRECTION, and why it is absorbed as a part: gating on unverified prices is D633's sin at one remove. pds-scratch-target_test.sh's own shipped row says "Hermeticity on a runner WITHOUT local Postgres is unproven here" - gating it is a day-one red on a foreign runner, the identical trap wave 44 documented for sheet-grid-js.yml. Rival C survives as exactly ONE new door: the one whose price and green I measured myself today.

blocks.text: Why the winner won

content.value: The spine plus the debts, with hetzner-offline as the one new door, is the only direction in which the wish's own item 2 does not manufacture the next wave's finding. It applies the epic's law to the epic's newest artifact, which is what every wave of this epic has actually been about. And it converts "spend the column" from a slogan into something that is safe to do more than once.

blocks.text: The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

content.value: THE ATTACK: "You are reopening a slice that shipped 11/12 with run evidence and rc=0 on main, on a distinction - 'measured' versus 'cached with provenance' - that is philosophy, not a defect. Nobody is harmed by a three-day-old CPU figure. This is the fifth consecutive wave arguing about a column, which is precisely what wave 44 ended."

That attack has real force, and the wave absorbs it by refusing to argue and making it a RUN. The spine ships only if the verify round can demonstrate, by mutation against a real tree, a case where the shipped census prints a number or a class the tree contradicts. I already hold one candidate - the hetzner row's wrong-arm evidence - and this wave's own slices manufacture two more. IF THE VERIFIERS CANNOT MAKE THE SHIPPED CENSUS PRINT A FALSEHOOD AGAINST A REAL TREE, THE SPINE IS CUT AND THIS WAVE BECOMES RIVAL A. That is the fail-before condition, declared before the fleet flies, and it is the honest version of "derive, never transcribe" turned on my own direction.

Second-order absorption, as a criterion rather than a hope: the design must not balloon the census's own price. A content hash per row is one shasum across 20 files - milliseconds. Re-running cheap dispositions is opt-in and threshold-printed, never on --check's default path.

blocks.text: Survey digest - 15 reports, and the fail-before is already satisfied

content.value: DIGEST COMPLETE. The wave's declared FAIL-BEFORE - 'if the verify round cannot make the shipped census print a falsehood against a real tree, the spine is CUT' - was satisfied TWICE during the SURVEY, independently, by two agents who did not talk to each other. price-provenance-audit replaced the 610-line scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh with a two-line 'exit 0' and the BYTE-IDENTICAL shipped census still printed 'THROUGH CPU=1.45+3.00=4.45s ... (76 checks, 0 failures)', rc=0, ERRORS 0. census-rot-mutation did the same at 32699 bytes -> 105 bytes and diffed the output against a captured baseline: EMPTY. The spine stands. It does not need the verify round to earn its place; the verify round now exists to size it and to keep it from pricing the census out of its own door.

Three independent confirmations of the direction's ground truth, all by run: (1) the census's whole run costs ~2.4-2.8 s CPU while printing a 40.33 s row - arithmetically impossible, no further argument needed; (2) grep over the 835-line script returns ZERO timing primitives, hashes or date arithmetic in executable position - every '/usr/bin/time' occurrence is INSIDE a quoted price string; (3) the verb set is exactly --check | --selftest | --list-refs | --help. There is no --measure.

blocks.text: What the survey ESTABLISHED (not inherited)

items.value: ALL THREE claimed rot classes fire against a real tree. STALE PRICE: deleting a whole 76-check harness leaves the output byte-identical. STALE DISPOSITION EVIDENCE: neutralising pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh to rc=0 leaves CONTENT-RED printed verbatim with its 2026-08-03 stamp. ORPHANED DISPOSITION: giving the hetzner runner both legs flips it to THROUGH, moves 4 of 20 -> 5 of 20, and the ENVIRONMENT row asserting a credential refusal goes silently unread - and the census's own --selftest reports 8 PASS / 0 FAIL over the orphan.

A FOURTH ROT CLASS, found twice independently: EVIDENCE-ABOUT-THE-WRONG-ARM. The hetzner row cites '--selftest rc=3' while the script's own :13 and :964 declare --selftest-offline 'the CREDENTIAL-FREE arm and the CI-able gate'; the scratch-target row's blocker clause names hermeticity, which is now REFUTED. No hash and no re-run catches either - only reading the cited file:line against the claim does. Two instances is an invariant, not two typos.

A FIFTH GAP the direction did not name: the PRICE shape validator at census :549-558 lives inside the terminal ELSE branch. The four rows that are actually THROUGH the door get NO price shape check at all. The most-gated rows are the least-validated.

#9380's leg A ADMITS A FRAUDULENT THROUGH, proven end-to-end with a price attached. Root cause is five lines: the taint-harvest loop comment-filters L[i], the EXECUTION scan splices L[j] (j=i+1,i+2) in RAW. Any comment within two lines below any System.cmd satisfies predicate 3. A second shape needs no comment at all. The shipped selftest is green because its fraud fixture forgets to BIND - it tests the wrong fraudster.

#9377's shipped NON-VACUITY block IS a stub - it asserts a constant defined in the test file itself, plus two verbatim duplicates of earlier tests. But the FILE is not vacuous: test 2 reads persisted bytes back and discriminates the new arm by a distinct flash string. The builder's hand mutation IS recorded in the closed task's criterion-4 evidence (paper.ex:152 prefixed 'false and ', RED at test line 264 naming ESCALATED). The proof was performed and never shipped. The @moduledoc's claim that the escalation is 'reproduced BY RUN in the same file' is a FALSE SENTENCE ON MERGED CODE.

--selftest-offline is genuinely credential-free and hermetic: rc=0 x3 under env -i with empty HOME, prints '0 hetzner/hcloud variables', zero repo residue. Its price is 1.97-2.30 s CPU, NOT the 3.75-3.90 s the deferred task's brief carries - a ~1.7x stale figure inside the very wave whose thesis is stale figures.

pds-scratch-target_test.sh's hermeticity blocker is REFUTED by run: 32 PASS / 0 FAIL with 10 denial-shim Postgres binaries on PATH, and again under env -i. Its price has been 4.30 s (charter), 8.91 s (census) and 9.45 s (re-measured) across three waves. It is a CANDIDATE DOOR, not a price refusal - and the census contains NO numeric price threshold anywhere, so 'PRICE' is a class with no predicate. The revealed cut sits unstated in (4.45, 8.91].

pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs's UNMEASURED-LOCAL is an UNPAID measurement, not an honest gap: the three gated arms cost 28.97 + 32.19 + 5.38 = 66.54 s CPU. That makes it the MOST EXPENSIVE door in the inventory, 1.65x pds-ledger-census_test.sh. D646's fan-out blindness does NOT apply - the gated arms spawn no child BEAM, and the outer meter READ HIGHER than the census's own internal self-report, the inverse signature of concealment.

pds-ledger-census_test.sh is 144 checks (D637's 107 is dead) and its price is ~100% dead weight: 144 x 'census --help' with zero fixture work costs MORE than the whole suite. A two-line lazy-urllib change cuts it 29% CPU with 144/144 still passing. Do not tier it - cut its boot cost and it stops being a tiering case.

The charter sweep's arrival count has moved a THIRD time: 41 -> 45 -> 59 (49 distinct slugs), because the IDIOM vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER in-process - a bigger charter changes the LENS, not just the corpus. Its --selftest is a HOSTAGE of the CONTENT-RED: it fails at its FIRST gate and never reaches any of its three lens assertions. And its fail-open at :203 was REPRODUCED - a dead bp shim produces NOT-A-TASK verdict lines byte-identical to an honest run, with a live-doc control dropping NOT-A-TASK from 16 to 1 to prove the branch is not dead code. The false absence is PERSISTED to confirm.json.

The lv_verdict '?' reorder is correctly ruled out, for a STRONGER reason than wave 44 gave: a '?' spec supplies no join key, so hoisting the residual arm widens BY PROXY - the exact inverse of the residual block's own PDS-D572 doctrine. The buildable half is different work: SPLIT arm 2 (one class name over two disjoint predicates) and PRINT the unnameable-spec count as a derived BOUND. Today N=0 by run across all 11 live plugin specs.

The criterion-venue defect is 11 criteria across 7 of 15 w43/w44 slices, not two. On BUILT slices: 4 of 7 PR-body criteria left permanently unstamped, 2 rescued by silently re-venuing. And the justification stamped on both rescued rows - 'the commit message becomes the PR body' - is FALSE: bp-epic-cycle.workflow.js:870 opens PRs with an explicit --body, which suppresses gh's commit autofill.

content.value: WHAT STALLED — nothing. Three slices were deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, each on a hard dependency that has to merge first: pds-w45-census-ledger-integrity (round 2, after #9434 — same file, ~180 lines move), pds-w45-price-provenance (round 3, after round 2 — same file, built on top), pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door (round 4, after both — it needs the retire shape and --measure those rounds create). Their tasks are open, unclaimed and 0/N met, which is the honest state, not a stall.

blocks.text: THE TWO FINDINGS REVIEW ADDED, AND THE RULES THEY BUY

content.value: PDS-D664 — A REPAIRED PREDICATE CARRIES ITS OLD DEFECT FOR EXACTLY ONE LINE. arg_span replaced the three-line proximity window with a real paren-balance walk, and the three fraud shapes flipped as designed. It still returned the whole CLOSING LINE, so "System.cmd(...) ; File.regular?(@fraud)" — a token named after the closing paren, on the call's own line — still read as argument-list membership: bound, never executed, THROUGH with a price. One line of the old window living inside the new predicate, past a 13-arm green selftest. THE RULE: when you replace a window with a boundary, the boundary is where the window's last residue hides — test the token that sits just OUTSIDE the new edge, not only the ones that sat inside the old one.

PDS-D665 — BOTH LEGS OR NEITHER APPLIES TO EVIDENCE STRINGS, NOT ONLY TO DECLARED PATH SETS. The wish states the both-legs law for the hetzner slice's ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry. It bit somewhere nobody named: the sweep's own fix makes --selftest rc=0, which turns the door census row whose evidence quotes "--selftest rc=1" into a stale receipt the moment it merges — on the instrument whose entire subject is receipts that lie. The builder was fenced out of the census and correctly recorded the correction in two durable venues rather than reaching across the fence. Review co-landed the one-line row edit on the SAME branch: a behaviour and the receipt describing it merge together or not at all. A fence that splits those two has to be closed by whoever holds both, and the fix belongs on the branch that causes the drift.

blocks.text: LEDGER AUDIT — three fixes, and one defect the audit itself surfaced

content.value: Every slice task was claimed before work, stamped mid-claim with real evidence rather than batched at the end, and left in_progress with only the merge-gated row open — with one exception, now fixed. Tasks outside this wave were not touched.

items.value: pds-w45-criterion-venue sat at lifecycle_status=open while HOLDING a live claim with 7 criteria stamped — a worked, claimed row reading as unstarted on every board. Re-claimed as the reviewer (epoch 9) so the lifecycle matches reality: in_progress, 8/9 met.

pds-w45-criterion-venue[4] ("The lead-owned merge-gated row ... is EXPLICITLY EXEMPTED and is left byte-identical") was PROVEN but UNSTAMPED: bp task stamp refuses any --criterion-text containing the substring "merge-gated", so a row that DESCRIBES the gated row is refused as though it WERE one. Re-derived independently (cmp on the two lines: IDENTICAL, 189 bytes; full-file diff one hunk 137a138) and stamped with the override, with that provenance in the evidence.

pds-w45-census-row-check-evidence — filed by the sweep builder as follow-up work — was DONE by the reviewer commit on the sweep branch. Claimed, its single criterion stamped with the new row verbatim plus four runs, and left in_progress: it closes when #9441 merges.

The stamp-guard defect is NOT newly filed: it duplicates pds-w27-bl-stamp-guard-substring-false-positive (wave 27, still open, root-caused to internal/cli/tasks_stamp_cmd.go). A new task was created, the server flagged the duplicate, and it was DELETED rather than left to double-count the backlog. The recurrence is recorded here instead.

Three follow-ups filed BY THE BUILDERS are published children of the epic and honest: pds-w45-argspan-sigil-and-silent-bound (sigil-blind blanking, the silent 40-line bound), task-ac55ff2388510d67 (the ladder's :stale arm is a NO-OP and nothing proves it), pds-w45-census-row-check-evidence (above).

blocks.text: GRADE — A

content.value: WHAT EARNS IT. The wave paid all three items the wish named and paid them in the order the dependencies allow. The second-review debt on #9377 is now discharged BY THE MERGING ARTIFACT rather than by a reviewer's hand mutation — that was the live gap on merged code, and it is the difference between "someone proved it once" and "the repo proves it every run". The ladder slice is the wave's best work: it recognised that its own headline number is evidence of nothing, said so in the printed output, and shipped the only discriminator that exists as a selftest case verified in both directions. The sweep slice reproduced its fail-open with the CORRECT oracle after the criterion named the wrong one, and closed it with the discriminator that was already on the wire. Four of five slices refuted something in their own dispatch by run — the eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth consecutive refutations — and each wrote the correction into the artifact instead of quietly satisfying a figure that does not exist.

WHAT KEEPS IT OFF A+. Two of the five needed a reviewer fix to a predicate that had just been tightened, and in both cases the defect was one step past where the builder stopped looking: the first occurrence rather than the only occurrence, the closing line rather than the closing paren. Both slices had green, honest, non-vacuous selftests through the defect. The wave also left three real UNPROVEN arms shipping green by print rather than by mutation — the ladder's :stale filter, arg_span's "every call opening on the line" clause, and its 40-line bound — each filed, none closed, and each is exactly the shape this epic exists to refuse. And every price and timing in this wave is LOCAL: no PDS door has yet run on a foreign runner, so the price column remains an instrument calibrated against one host.

NOT A CRITICISM, ON THE RECORD: the wish's item 4 (the unbuilt "?" variable-bound decline) was RULED OUT with a reason, not quietly dropped — PDS-D661 — and the ladder slice printed declined_live=0 as a BOUND on the sentence instead, derived THROUGH lvs_joinable?/1 so the number cannot drift from the predicate it describes. Ruling it out was the right half of "finish it or rule it out".

blocks.text: WHAT THE NEXT WAVE TAKES

content.value: MERGE ORDER FIRST. The five round-1 PRs are file-disjoint except that #9434 and #9441 both touch scripts/pds-door-census.sh — #9434 in the classifier and the selftest, #9441 at line 123 of PDS_DOOR_DISPOSITIONS only — so either order merges without a conflict. Then dispatch the deferred slices STRICTLY in dependency order, re-deriving every anchor at each merged base, because each one moves the file the next one reads.

One standing debt outranks all of them for credibility: NO pds door has ever been measured on a foreign runner, so every figure in the price column is a loaded local mac.

THE SECOND-REVIEWER DEBT, NAMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED DISCHARGED. #9433 is a HIGH-FLIP-RISK slice on a live grant/tenancy door, and this workflow spawns exactly ONE reviewer — so the independent second pass is a MANUAL LEAD STEP before merge. I re-derived the substitution from source and mutation-proved my own guard, but a genuinely independent pair of eyes on the authorization judgment is still owed.
